name: Jameson JA-34 Link
title: Jameson JA-34 Link: Pole Pruner Replacement Part
meta: The Jameson JA-34 link is a replacement part for Jameson pole pruner heads. Swap a bent or worn link and get a clean, full-stroke cut back on the job.
tagline: A small replacement link that keeps a Jameson pole pruner head cutting cleanly.
summary: The Jameson JA-34 link is a replacement part for the linkage on Jameson pole pruner heads. When the link bends or the holes wear oval, the blade loses stroke and starts crushing instead of cutting, and a new link is the cheap fix.
highlights: Replacement link for Jameson pole pruner heads
Restores full blade travel and a clean cut
Far cheaper than a new pruner head
Worth keeping a spare in the pole kit

p: A pole pruner takes a beating. It gets dropped in the bed of the truck, yanked through crotches and twisted when a limb pinches the blade. The link between the lever and the blade is one of the parts that pays for that. Once it bends even slightly, the blade stops closing fully against the hook and you get chewed, half-cut limbs that have to be torn off.
Check the link whenever the cut feels rough or the head hangs open. Look for a bend, cracks around the holes or holes that have worn oval. Any of those means it is time for a new one.

Pull the bolt or pin that holds the old link, note how it sits, and fit the new JA-34 the same way round. Use new hardware if the old bolt is worn, snug it so the parts move freely without slop, and work the head through a few full strokes before going back to work.
Confirm the part number against your pruner head before ordering, since Jameson has made several heads over the years. For complete heads, poles and kits, see our poles and pole kits range.

faq.q: How do I know the JA-34 link fits my pruner?
faq.a: Check the part number in your Jameson parts diagram or compare against the old link. If in doubt, measure hole spacing before ordering.

faq.q: Should I replace the spring at the same time?
faq.a: If the head has seen heavy use, it is worth checking the spring and bolts while it is apart. A tired spring slows the blade return.

name: Jameson Big Mouth Pruner Spring
title: Jameson Big Mouth Pruner Spring: Replacement Part
meta: Replacement Jameson Big Mouth pruner spring to bring back a fast, positive blade return. Cheap fix for a pole pruner head that hangs closed or opens slowly.
tagline: A fresh return spring for the Jameson Big Mouth pole pruner head.
summary: The Jameson Big Mouth pruner spring is the return spring that pulls the blade back open after each cut. When it weakens or breaks, the head hangs closed and you end up shaking the pole to reset it, which slows every cut.
highlights: Return spring for the Jameson Big Mouth pruner head
Restores quick, positive blade opening
Inexpensive alternative to a new head
Easy swap with basic hand tools

p: The Big Mouth is built for bigger bites than a standard pole pruner, and the spring works hard to open that wider jaw every time you let off the rope. Over a season of clearing lines or lifting canopies, springs lose tension, stretch or snap at the hook.
A tired spring shows up as a blade that drifts open slowly, or one that doesn't open far enough to get over the next limb. Swapping it takes a few minutes and makes the tool feel new again.

Lay the head on a bench, note how the old spring is hooked, and remove it. Hook the new spring in the same position, then run the blade through several full strokes to make sure it opens fully and closes without binding.

While the head is apart, check the blade edge, the bolts and the pulley for wear. Keep a spare spring in the truck if Big Mouth pruners are in daily use. More pole parts are in our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Will this spring fit a standard Jameson pruner?
faq.a: It is made for the Big Mouth head. Standard and heavy duty Jameson heads use their own springs, so match the spring to the head.

faq.q: How often should I replace the spring?
faq.a: Replace it whenever the blade returns slowly or not at all. Heavy daily users often swap it every season.

name: Jameson Heavy Duty Pruner Spring
title: Jameson Heavy Duty Pruner Spring: Replacement
meta: Jameson heavy duty pruner spring for pole pruner heads. Replace a stretched or broken return spring so the blade snaps open fast and the head cuts cleanly.
tagline: Replacement return spring for Jameson heavy duty pole pruner heads.
summary: The Jameson heavy duty pruner spring returns the blade to the open position after each pull on a Jameson pole pruner. A worn spring makes the head sluggish, and a broken one leaves you flicking the pole to reopen the jaw.
highlights: Return spring for Jameson heavy duty pruner heads
Brings back fast blade return
Low-cost maintenance part
Simple bench swap
specs: Jameson heavy duty pruner heads (confirm model)

p: Pole pruners get used hard on line clearance, orchard and storm work. The spring is the part that keeps the blade ready for the next cut, and it is usually the first thing to tire out. If the blade opens slowly, stops partway or the spring is visibly stretched with gaps between coils, replace it.
Running a pruner with a bad spring wastes time on every cut and puts more strain on your shoulders, since you end up working the rope and the pole to reset the jaw.

Note how the old spring hooks to the blade and the head, then fit the new one in the same spot. Work the head through a few full strokes. The blade should open crisply and close fully against the hook.
While you are there, check the blade for nicks and the bolts for wear. Confirm the spring matches your head before ordering. For poles and complete pruners, browse our poles and pole kits range.

faq.q: Is the heavy duty spring the same as the Big Mouth spring?
faq.a: No. Each Jameson head uses its own spring, so order the one that matches your pruner.

faq.q: Can I stretch an old spring to get more tension?
faq.a: No. A stretched or fatigued spring should be replaced, not adjusted.

name: Jameson Saw Head Lower Black Bolts
title: Jameson Saw Head Lower Black Bolts: Replacement
h1: Jameson Saw Head Lower Black Bolts
meta: Replacement lower black bolts for Jameson pole saw heads. Keep the blade tight on the head so the pole saw cuts straight and doesn't wobble or loosen in use.
tagline: Replacement lower bolts that hold the blade tight on a Jameson pole saw head.
summary: These Jameson saw head lower black bolts are the replacement fasteners for the lower blade mount on Jameson pole saw heads. Worn or lost bolts let the blade rock on the head, and a wobbling pole saw blade binds, wanders and wears fast.
highlights: Replacement lower bolts for Jameson pole saw heads
Keeps the blade tight and true
Handy spares for blade changes in the field
Black finish to match the original hardware

p: Pole saw blades get swapped more often than any other part on a pole kit. Every blade change is a chance to drop a bolt in the grass or round off a head. Having spare lower bolts in the truck means a lost fastener doesn't end the pole work for the day.
Loose or worn bolts are also a cutting problem. If the blade can shift even a little, the kerf wanders, the blade binds in the cut and the saw head takes the stress.

Line the blade up on the head, fit the bolts and tighten them evenly so the blade sits flat. Check them again after the first few cuts, since a new blade can settle. Replace bolts with stripped threads or rounded heads rather than reusing them.
Confirm these match your Jameson saw head before ordering. For poles, saw heads and kits, see our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Do these come as a set?
faq.a: Pack contents can vary by supplier, so check the listing for quantity before ordering.

faq.q: Can I use hardware store bolts instead?
faq.a: Matching bolts keep the blade seated as designed. Odd sizes or lengths can let the blade shift or snag the head, so use the correct parts.

name: Male Ferrule for Sectional Poles
title: Male Ferrule for Sectional Pruning Poles
meta: Replacement pole male ferrule for sectional fiberglass pruning poles. Repair a worn or damaged joint so pole sections lock together firmly again on the job.
tagline: A replacement male joint fitting for sectional pruning and pole saw poles.
summary: A pole male ferrule is the fitting on the end of a sectional pole that slides into the next section's female socket. When it gets bent, cracked or worn loose, the joint wobbles or won't lock, and replacing the ferrule can save the pole.
highlights: Male end fitting for sectional poles
Repairs loose, bent or cracked joints
Saves replacing a whole pole section
Match the ferrule to your pole diameter and system
specs: Sectional pruning and pole saw poles
Match to your pole brand and diameter

p: Sectional poles let you build reach as you need it, and the joints are what make that work. The male ferrule carries the lock button or locking feature and takes the bending load where two sections meet. A damaged ferrule makes the whole pole feel sloppy and can let a section slip apart overhead.
Common causes are dropping the pole on a joint, prying with a pole saw stuck in a cut and dirt grinding away at the fit over time.

Ferrules are not universal. Match the replacement to your pole brand, outside diameter and locking style, and compare with the old one before ordering. Follow the pole maker's instructions for removing the old ferrule and bonding or pinning the new one.
If the fiberglass behind the ferrule is cracked or splintered, replace the section. Never use a damaged pole near energized lines. Browse our poles and pole kits for complete poles and kits.

faq.q: Will this ferrule fit any pole?
faq.a: No. Ferrules are sized to specific pole systems and diameters, so confirm the match before buying.

faq.q: Can I repair a cracked pole with a new ferrule?
faq.a: Only if the pole tube itself is sound. Cracked fiberglass means the section should be retired.

name: Marvin Cap Screw, Washer and Nut
title: Marvin Cap Screw, Washer and Nut: Pruner Hardware
h1: Marvin Cap Screw, Washer and Nut
meta: Marvin cap screw, washer and nut set for Marvin pole pruner and saw heads. Replace worn or lost hardware so the head stays tight and the blade moves freely.
tagline: Replacement fastener set for Marvin pole pruner and saw heads.
summary: The Marvin cap screw, washer and nut set replaces the fasteners on Marvin pole tools. Worn or lost hardware lets the blade wobble, and a sloppy pivot leaves ragged cuts and stresses the head.
highlights: Cap screw, washer and nut for Marvin heads
Restores a tight, smooth pivot
Cheap insurance against lost hardware
Good spare to keep in the pole kit
specs: Marvin pole tool heads (confirm position and model)

p: Marvin pruner and saw heads are simple, tough tools, and the hardware that holds them together is what keeps them cutting right. Vibration, blade changes and the odd drop work fasteners loose over time. A worn screw or missing washer can let the blade shift off the hook, which turns a clean bypass cut into a crushed, torn stub.
Replacing the full set at once keeps everything matched and avoids mixing worn and new parts.

Remove the old hardware, clean the pivot area and fit the new cap screw with the washer in the same order as original. Tighten the nut until the blade moves freely without side play. Run the head through several strokes and recheck before use.
Check the part position on your Marvin parts diagram before ordering. More pole parts and heads are in our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Which Marvin heads does this fit?
faq.a: Marvin uses this style of hardware on several heads. Compare against your parts list or the old fastener to confirm.

faq.q: How tight should the nut be?
faq.a: Snug enough to remove side play while the blade still opens and closes freely.

name: Marvin PH4 Pruner Spring
title: Marvin PH4 Pruner Spring: Replacement Return Spring
meta: Marvin pruner spring, part PH4, for Marvin pole pruner heads. Replace a weak or broken spring so the blade opens fast and the pruner is ready for each cut.
tagline: Replacement return spring for Marvin pole pruner heads.
summary: The Marvin pruner spring, part PH4, returns the blade to open after each cut on a Marvin pole pruner. Once it weakens, the head hangs closed and every cut takes longer.
highlights: Return spring for Marvin pole pruner heads
Part number PH4
Restores crisp blade return
Inexpensive, quick swap

body.h: A small part that sets the pace
p: A pole pruner is only as fast as its spring. When the spring is fresh, you pull, cut, let off and the jaw is open for the next limb. When it is worn, you are shaking the pole and waiting. On a long day of clearance pruning, that adds up.
Replace the spring when it shows gaps between coils at rest, the hook end is worn thin, or the blade no longer opens fully on its own.

Note how the old spring hooks in, remove it and fit the PH4 in the same position. Work the blade by hand to confirm a full, smooth return. While the head is open, look over the blade edge, pulley and pivot hardware.
Keep a spare spring with the pole kit if you run Marvin heads daily. For heads, adapters and poles, see our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Does the PH4 spring fit Marvin bull pruners?
faq.a: Check your parts diagram. Marvin heads differ, so match the spring to the head you own.

faq.q: Why does my new spring feel stiffer?
faq.a: A fresh spring has full tension. That is normal and is what makes the blade snap back open.

name: Marvin Pole End Cap
title: Marvin Pole End Cap: Replacement Pole Butt Cap
meta: Marvin pole end cap for the butt of a pruning or pole saw pole. Keeps dirt and water out of the tube and protects the end when the pole is grounded on the job.
tagline: A replacement butt cap that seals and protects the bottom end of a Marvin pole.
summary: The Marvin pole end cap fits the bottom end of a pruning or pole saw pole. It keeps dirt, water and debris out of the tube and takes the wear when the pole is set on the ground between cuts.
highlights: Caps the butt end of the pole
Keeps moisture and dirt out of the tube
Protects the pole end from wear
Easy replacement for a lost or split cap

p: The butt of a pole spends its life being set down in dirt, gravel and wet grass. Without a cap, the open end chews up and packs with mud, and moisture can get inside the tube. A missing cap is easy to ignore, but the damage builds up and it shortens pole life.
A good end cap also gives a cleaner contact point when you plant the pole to steady a cut or rest your arms.
Clean and dry the pole end, then press or fit the new cap until it seats fully. Check it periodically, since caps can work loose or split from impact. Replace a cracked cap rather than taping it.

Inspect the pole itself while you are at it. Splintered fiberglass or deep gouges mean the section should be retired, especially for any work near power lines. Browse our poles and pole kits for poles and kits.

faq.q: Will this cap fit other pole brands?
faq.a: Possibly, if the outside diameter matches, but it is made for Marvin poles. Measure before ordering.

faq.q: Is the end cap required?
faq.a: It is not structural, but it protects the pole and keeps contaminants out, which helps the pole last.

name: Marvin Pruner Head Adaptor
title: Marvin Pruner Head Adaptor: Mount Pruner to Pole
meta: Marvin pruner head adaptor for mounting a Marvin pole pruner head to a pole. Replace a cracked or loose adaptor and get a solid, wobble-free connection back.
tagline: The fitting that joins a Marvin pole pruner head to the top of the pole.
summary: The Marvin pruner head adaptor is the fitting that connects a Marvin pole pruner head to the top section of a pole. A worn or cracked adaptor lets the head twist and rock, which ruins cut control overhead.
highlights: Mounts a Marvin pruner head to a pole
Replaces a cracked, loose or worn adaptor
Restores solid head alignment
Good to have when building or repairing a pole kit

p: The adaptor takes every twist and pry the pruner sees and passes it into the pole. That makes it a wear item. If the head turns on the pole, clicks under load or sits crooked, the adaptor is often the culprit.
A solid head matters for accuracy. When you are reaching for a crossing limb 15 feet up, you need the blade to go where you aim it, not rotate off the branch.

Remove the head from the old adaptor, then follow Marvin's instructions to take the adaptor off the pole and fit the new one. Confirm it is fully seated and fastened before reinstalling the head. Check the pull rope route so it runs freely past the new adaptor.
Make sure the adaptor matches your pole diameter. For poles, heads and kits, see our poles and pole kits range.

faq.q: Is the pruner adaptor the same as the saw head adaptor?
faq.a: No. Marvin makes separate adaptors for pruner heads and saw heads, so order the one for your head.

faq.q: Can I fit a Marvin head to another brand's pole?
faq.a: Only if the adaptor matches that pole's diameter and fitting. Check before buying.

name: Marvin Saw Head Adaptor
title: Marvin Saw Head Adaptor: Mount Saw Head to Pole
meta: Marvin saw head adaptor for mounting a Marvin pole saw head to a pole. Replace a worn or cracked fitting so the saw stays aligned and doesn't twist in the cut.
tagline: The fitting that holds a Marvin pole saw head square on the pole.
summary: The Marvin saw head adaptor connects a Marvin pole saw head to the top of a pole. When it cracks or wears loose, the saw head twists in the cut, the blade binds and you lose control of where the kerf goes.
highlights: Mounts a Marvin saw head to a pole
Keeps the blade aligned with the pole
Replaces a cracked or sloppy fitting
Useful for building or repairing pole saw kits

p: Pole saws are pushed, pulled and pried constantly. Every time a blade pinches and gets wrenched free, the adaptor takes the load. Over time it can crack or loosen on the pole, and you will feel it as play between the head and the pole or a saw that rotates when you start a cut.
A tight adaptor keeps the blade in line with your stroke, so the saw tracks straight and you spend less energy fighting it.

Remove the saw head, take off the old adaptor following Marvin's instructions and fit the new one fully seated and fastened. Reinstall the saw head and blade, then check that nothing moves when you twist the head by hand.
Match the adaptor to your pole diameter before ordering. Browse our poles and pole kits for poles and complete kits.

faq.q: Will this adaptor fit a Marvin pruner head?
faq.a: No. Use the Marvin pruner head adaptor for pruners.

faq.q: How do I know the adaptor is worn?
faq.a: Twist the head by hand. Any rotation, clicking or visible cracks mean it is time to replace it.

name: Silky Elastic Leg Straps
title: Silky Elastic Leg Straps for Saw Scabbards
meta: Silky elastic leg straps hold a long saw scabbard against your thigh so it doesn't swing or snag while climbing, walking brush or working off a ladder.
tagline: Elastic thigh straps that keep a long Silky scabbard from swinging.
summary: Silky leg straps are elastic straps that hold the bottom of a saw scabbard against your thigh. On longer saws the scabbard tip swings, catches on brush and slaps your leg, and a leg strap stops that.
highlights: Holds a scabbard tip against the thigh
Stops swinging and snagging
Elastic for comfort while climbing and walking
Replacement or upgrade for Silky scabbards

p: A long curved hand saw rides on the saddle or belt, and the scabbard hangs well down your leg. Without anything holding it, the tip catches on branches as you move through the canopy and bangs your knee on every step on the ground. A leg strap anchors it so the saw stays where you expect it when you reach down to draw it.
The elastic gives as your leg bends, so it holds the scabbard without cutting off circulation or limiting movement on a climb.

Attach the strap to the scabbard's lower slot or loop, then wrap and fasten it around your thigh snug enough to stop the swing. Check the elastic for fraying or loss of stretch and replace it when it no longer holds.
Keep the strap clear of your climbing system and lanyard. For pole saws, poles and kits, see our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Do the straps fit all Silky scabbards?
faq.a: They are made for Silky scabbards with a leg strap attachment point. Check that your scabbard has one.

faq.q: Will a leg strap get in the way while climbing?
faq.a: Adjusted snug and routed clear of your hitch and lanyard, most climbers find it reduces snags rather than adding them.

name: Phoenix Pole Saw Head
title: Phoenix Saw Head for Pole Saws
meta: The Phoenix saw head mounts a pruning blade to a sectional pole for reaching limbs from the ground. Check blade and pole fit, then cut clean overhead with less strain.
tagline: A pole saw head that turns a sectional pole into an overhead pruning saw.
summary: The Phoenix saw head is a pole saw head that clamps a pruning saw blade to the top of a pole, so you can cut limbs overhead from the ground. It is the business end of a pole saw setup and the part that takes the most abuse.
highlights: Mounts a pruning blade to a pole
For overhead cuts from the ground or a bucket
Replaces a cracked or worn saw head
Check blade bolt pattern and pole fit before buying
specs: Mounting a pole saw blade to a pole

body.h: Where it fits in a pole kit
p: A pole saw is three things: the pole, the head and the blade. The head holds the blade at the right angle and carries every push and pull into the pole. When a head cracks, the bolt holes wear or the pole fitting loosens, the blade wobbles and the saw stops tracking straight.
A fresh saw head brings back a stiff, predictable tool for lifting canopies, clearing deadwood and cutting back from structures where you can't climb or don't need to.

Saw heads are not universal. Confirm the head fits your pole's diameter and connection style, and that your blade's bolt pattern matches the head. Tighten blade bolts evenly and recheck them after the first few cuts.
Never use a pole saw near energized lines unless you are qualified and the tool is rated for that work. Compare other heads and blades in our pole saws and scabbards range.

faq.q: Will the Phoenix saw head fit my pole?
faq.a: Check the pole diameter and connection type against the head's listing. Fit varies between pole systems.

faq.q: Does it come with a blade?
faq.a: Saw heads are often sold without a blade. Check the listing and match the blade bolt pattern.

name: Silky Saw Head for Standard Poles
title: Silky Pole Saw Head for Standard Poles
h1: Silky Saw Head for Standard Poles
meta: Silky pole saw head that fits standard sectional poles, so you can run a Silky blade on the pole system you already own. Clean, fast pull-stroke cuts overhead.
tagline: Run a Silky pole saw blade on a standard sectional pole.
summary: This Silky pole saw head lets you mount a Silky pole saw blade on a standard pruning pole instead of a Silky telescoping pole. If your crew already runs sectional fiberglass poles, it is a way to get Silky's pull-stroke cutting on the same kit.
highlights: Mounts a Silky blade on standard poles
Pull-stroke cutting for fast overhead work
Use with the poles you already carry
Confirm blade model and pole fit
specs: Silky pole saw blades (sold separately unless listed)

p: Silky pole saw blades have a reputation for cutting fast on the pull stroke with impulse-hardened teeth. Many crews like that blade but prefer the reach, stiffness or dielectric features of the sectional poles they already own. This head bridges the two.
It is also a tidy way to standardize: one pole system on the truck, with saw and pruner heads that swap as the job changes from lifting canopy to clearing deadwood.

Fit the head to the top pole section and bolt the blade on evenly. Check that nothing twists before you start cutting. Let the pull stroke do the work, and make an undercut on heavier limbs so the bark doesn't tear back toward the trunk.
Keep the blade in a scabbard when not cutting. See more heads, blades and covers in our pole saws and scabbards section.

faq.q: Which Silky blades fit this head?
faq.a: Check the listing for compatible Silky pole saw blades and match the bolt pattern.

faq.q: Can I use it on a telescoping pole?
faq.a: It is made for standard sectional pole fittings. Telescoping poles usually take their own heads.

name: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard for 13" Hook Tip Blades
title: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard for 13" Hook Tip Blades
h1: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard for 13" Hook Tip Blades
meta: Weaver pole saw scabbard sized for 13 inch hook tip blades. Covers the teeth for transport and storage, protecting the blade, the truck and the crew.
tagline: A blade cover for 13 inch hook tip pole saw blades.
summary: The Weaver pole saw scabbard for 13 inch hook tip blades covers the teeth and hook of a pole saw blade when it is not cutting. It protects the blade's edge, the truck and anyone handling the poles.
highlights: Sized for 13 inch hook tip pole saw blades
Covers teeth and hook for transport
Protects crew hands and other gear
Weaver build for daily truck use

p: A pole saw blade rides in the truck or on the rack between jobs, and an uncovered blade is a hazard. It catches on rope bags, chews up tarps and slices hands when someone grabs the poles in a hurry. Teeth also dull fast when they rattle against steel and gravel.
A scabbard sized for the blade stays on during travel and keeps the hook tip from snagging anything on the way.

This version is cut for 13 inch blades with a hook tip. A scabbard that is too short leaves teeth exposed, and one made for a straight tip won't cover the hook properly. Measure your blade and check its tip shape before ordering.

Slide the scabbard on whenever the pole goes down for more than a moment, and keep it clean so grit doesn't wear the teeth. Weaver also makes a 16 inch version. Browse our pole saws and scabbards for more.

faq.q: Will this fit a 13 inch blade without a hook tip?
faq.a: It may, but it is shaped for hook tip blades. A straight tip blade may sit loose.

faq.q: Can I leave the scabbard on while carrying the pole on site?
faq.a: Yes, and you should. Remove it only when you are ready to cut.

name: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard for 16" Blades
title: Weaver 16" Pole Saw Scabbard: Blade Cover
h1: Weaver Pole Saw Scabbard for 16" Blades
meta: Weaver 16 pole saw scabbard sized for 16 inch blades. Keeps teeth covered in the truck and on site, so the blade stays sharp and nobody gets cut handling poles.
tagline: A blade cover sized for 16 inch pole saw blades.
summary: The Weaver 16 pole saw scabbard covers a 16 inch pole saw blade during transport and storage. Longer blades are more exposed and harder to manage, so a properly sized cover matters even more.
highlights: Sized for 16 inch pole saw blades
Protects teeth from dulling in transport
Keeps hands and gear clear of the edge
Weaver construction for daily use

p: A 16 inch pole saw blade gives you a big bite for heavier limbs, and a lot of exposed teeth when the pole is lying in the truck. Without a cover it snags rope, cuts into bags and puts the crew at risk when they grab poles off the rack.
The scabbard slides over the blade and stays on until you are ready to cut, protecting the teeth from rocks, steel and other tools.
Measure the blade before ordering. A scabbard that is too short leaves the tip teeth bare. If you run a 13 inch hook tip blade, Weaver makes a separate scabbard for that size.
Shake out sawdust and grit regularly so it doesn't grind the teeth in storage. Replace the scabbard if it splits along the edge. More covers and blades are in our pole saws and scabbards range.

faq.q: Will a 16 inch scabbard work on a 13 inch blade?
faq.a: It will cover it, but it will sit loose and can slide off. Use a scabbard sized to your blade.

faq.q: Does it fit hook tip blades?
faq.a: Check the tip shape of your blade against the scabbard. Weaver offers a version shaped for 13 inch hook tip blades.

name: Weaver Saw Scabbard with Pruner Pouch, Rubberized (HL-14)
keyword: weaver saw scabbard with pruner pouch
title: Weaver Saw Scabbard with Pruner Pouch, Rubberized
h1: Weaver Saw Scabbard with Pruner Pouch, Rubberized (HL-14)
meta: Weaver saw scabbard with pruner pouch, rubberized model HL-14. Carry a hand saw and hand pruners on one belt or saddle mount for faster pruning work aloft.
tagline: A rubberized hand saw scabbard with a built-in pouch for hand pruners.
summary: The Weaver saw scabbard with pruner pouch, rubberized model HL-14, carries a hand saw and a pair of hand pruners in one holster. Pruning climbers and ground crews get both cutting tools in one place on the saddle or belt.
highlights: Saw scabbard and pruner pouch in one
Rubberized construction
Model HL-14
Mounts on a saddle or work belt
Keeps both cutting tools within reach

p: Fine pruning means switching between hand pruners and a hand saw all day: pruners for small stems, saw for anything bigger. Carrying them in separate holsters crowds the saddle and puts tools on different sides. This Weaver scabbard keeps both together so you can reach for either without looking.
The rubberized build sheds sap and water and wipes clean, which matters when you are working in wet canopy or resinous conifers.

Mount it where your dominant hand falls naturally and where it stays clear of your hitch, lanyard and rope. Check that your saw's blade length and shape suit the scabbard before ordering, and that your pruners seat fully in the pouch.
Clear sawdust from the scabbard often so the teeth don't grind. Tether tools when working aloft. For more scabbards and saw covers, see our pole saws and scabbards section.

faq.q: What size saw does the HL-14 hold?
faq.a: Check the listing for blade length and shape, and compare with your saw before ordering.

faq.q: Can it go on a climbing saddle?
faq.a: Yes, it is made to mount on saddles and work belts. Keep it clear of life-support components.

name: Jameson 6' Hollow Core Poles
title: Jameson 6' Hollow Core Poles: Fiberglass Pole Sections
meta: Jameson hollow core poles in 6 foot fiberglass sections for pole saws and pruners. Lightweight, stiff and modular, so you build reach as each cut demands.
tagline: Six foot fiberglass pole sections for building Jameson pole saw and pruner kits.
summary: Jameson hollow core poles are fiberglass pole sections that lock together to build reach for pole saws and pole pruners. The 6 foot length is a handy size for the truck and lets you add reach in small steps.
highlights: 6 ft fiberglass pole sections
Hollow core for lighter weight
Sectional design builds reach as needed
Works with Jameson heads and fittings

p: A single long pole is awkward to transport and too much tool for low cuts. Sectional poles let you start short and add sections as you reach higher, so you carry only as much weight overhead as the cut needs. Six foot sections fit easily in most trucks and give fine control over total reach.

Hollow core poles are lighter than foam-filled poles, which makes a real difference over a day of overhead work. The trade-off is that the inside of the tube is open, so keep end caps on and keep the poles clean and dry.

Inspect each section before use for cracks, splinters, crushed walls and worn fittings. Store poles off the ground and out of the sun when possible, and wipe them down so dirt and moisture don't build up.

Do not assume any pole is safe near energized lines. Line clearance work requires tools rated and tested for it and workers qualified under the applicable standard. For heads and kits, see our poles and pole kits range.

faq.q: Can I mix 6 ft and 8 ft Jameson poles?
faq.a: Usually yes, if the fittings and diameters match. Check that the locking system is the same.

faq.q: What is the difference between hollow core and foam-filled?
faq.a: Hollow core poles are lighter. Foam-filled poles have a core that keeps moisture and debris out of the tube.

name: Jameson 8' B-Lite Poles
title: Jameson 8' B-Lite Poles: Fiberglass Pole Sections
meta: Jameson B-Lite poles in 8 foot fiberglass sections for pole saws and pruners. Lighter sections that build reach fast and ease shoulder strain on long days.
tagline: Eight foot B-Lite fiberglass pole sections for Jameson pole tool kits.
summary: Jameson B-Lite poles are 8 foot fiberglass pole sections built for pole saw and pruner kits where weight overhead matters. Longer sections mean fewer joints for a given reach, which keeps the pole stiffer and quicker to assemble.
highlights: 8 ft fiberglass pole sections
B-Lite series built to save weight
Fewer joints for a given reach
Works with Jameson heads and fittings

p: If most of your pole work is high, 8 foot sections get you there with fewer joints than 6 foot poles. Fewer joints means less flex and less play at the head, which helps when you are trying to place a pruner on a small stem near the top of your reach.
Weight is the other half. A pole held overhead all day wears out shoulders, and lighter sections let you keep cutting accurately later in the shift.
Check every section before use for cracks, splinters and worn locking fittings, and retire any damaged pole. Keep end caps on and store poles clean and dry.

Pole tools near power lines require qualified workers and tools rated and tested for that use. Do not assume a pole is safe because it is fiberglass. For heads, adapters and complete kits, see our poles and pole kits section.

faq.q: Do B-Lite poles work with my Jameson saw head?
faq.a: They are made for Jameson fittings. Confirm your head and pole connections match.

faq.q: Should I choose 6 ft or 8 ft sections?
faq.a: 8 ft sections reach higher with fewer joints. 6 ft sections are easier to carry and give finer control over length.

name: Jameson Foam-Filled Base Pole
title: Jameson Foam-Filled Base Pole for Pole Tools
meta: Jameson foam filled pole for the base section of a pole saw or pruner kit. Foam core keeps moisture and dirt out of the tube for a solid, durable bottom section.
tagline: A foam-core base section that anchors a Jameson sectional pole kit.
summary: The Jameson foam filled pole is a base section for sectional pole saw and pruner kits. Its foam core fills the inside of the fiberglass tube so moisture, dirt and debris can't collect inside, and the base end gives you a solid section to grip and plant.
highlights: Base section for sectional pole kits
Foam-filled fiberglass core
Keeps moisture and debris out of the tube
Works with Jameson fittings

p: A hollow pole is lighter, but the open tube can collect water, dirt and condensation over time. A foam core fills that space. That is why many utility and line clearance crews favor foam-filled poles, especially for the sections nearest the operator's hands.
As the base section, this is the pole you hold and the one that gets planted on the ground. A solid, sealed section there makes the whole kit feel more stable.

Inspect the pole before each use for cracks, gouges, a damaged surface and worn fittings. Keep it clean and stored dry. Many utilities require periodic electrical testing and specific ratings for poles used near energized lines, so check the markings and your employer's rules before any such work.
Never work near power lines unless you are qualified to do so under ANSI Z133 and your employer's program. For upper sections and heads, see our poles and pole kits range.

faq.q: Is a foam-filled pole safe to use near power lines?
faq.a: Only if it is rated and tested for that work and you are a qualified line clearance worker. Foam fill alone does not make a pole safe.

faq.q: Is a foam-filled pole heavier?
faq.a: Slightly, compared with a hollow section of the same length, which is why it is often used as the base.

name: Husqvarna Classic Hand Pruner
title: Husqvarna Classic Hand Pruner: Bypass Pruning Shears
meta: The Husqvarna Classic hand pruner is a bypass pruning shear for clean cuts on small live stems. A solid, affordable pick for climbers, ground crews and gardeners.
tagline: A straightforward bypass hand pruner for clean cuts on small stems.
summary: The Husqvarna Classic hand pruner is a bypass pruning shear for small live branches, suckers and fine detail work. It is the tool you reach for when a saw is overkill and a clean cut matters.
highlights: Bypass cutting action for clean live cuts
Sized for small stems and detail pruning
Handy for climbers and ground crews alike
Affordable everyday pruner

body.h: Where it fits on the job
p: Good pruning cuts start with the right tool. A bypass pruner slices like scissors, leaving a clean edge that seals well on live wood, unlike an anvil pruner that tends to crush. On a structural prune or a crown clean, a hand pruner handles suckers, water sprouts and small laterals faster than a saw.
Climbers carry one on the saddle for detail work, and ground crews use them for cleaning up shrubs, dressing cuts and trimming brush before it goes through the chipper.

Stay within the pruner's capacity. Twisting through a stem that is too big springs the blades and leaves a ragged cut. Switch to a hand saw for anything larger. Wipe sap off the blades after use, oil the pivot and keep the edge sharp with a fine stone.
Carry it in a holster or pouch when climbing and tether it if dropping it would put people below at risk. See more options in our pruners and loppers range.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna Classic a bypass or anvil pruner?
faq.a: It is a bypass pruner, which suits clean cuts on live wood.

faq.q: How big a branch can it cut?
faq.a: It is meant for small stems. Check the listed capacity and use a hand saw for larger branches.

name: Jameson Big Mouth Pruner Kit
title: Jameson Big Mouth Pruner Kit: Pole Pruner Set
meta: Jameson Big Mouth pruner kit with the wide-jaw pole pruner head and pole system. A ready-to-work set for bigger cuts overhead on clearance and canopy work.
tagline: A ready-to-work pole pruner kit built around Jameson's wide-jaw Big Mouth head.
summary: The Jameson Big Mouth pruner kit pairs the wide-jaw Big Mouth pole pruner head with poles and the parts you need to start cutting. It suits crews who want one order that covers overhead pruning without piecing together heads, adapters and rope.
highlights: Built around the Jameson Big Mouth pruner head
Wider jaw for larger stems than a standard head
Kit format, ready to assemble
Works with Jameson poles and accessories

p: Building a pole pruner from parts means matching the head, adapter, poles and pull rope. A kit takes care of that. You get a head, poles that fit it and the hardware to put them together, so you can go straight to cutting.

The Big Mouth head opens wider than a standard pole pruner, which lets it take bigger stems in one bite. That saves switching to a pole saw for every limb that is a little too thick for a standard head.

Set the hook over the limb, seat it fully and pull the rope with a steady stroke. Cut close to the branch collar without cutting into it. Use a pole saw for anything beyond the head's capacity rather than forcing it.

Check the spring, blade and rope regularly and keep spares. Pole tools near energized lines require qualified workers and properly rated tools. More pole pruners are in our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: What comes in the Jameson Big Mouth pruner kit?
faq.a: Kit contents vary by listing, so check what poles, rope and accessories are included before ordering.

faq.q: Can I add a pole saw to this kit?
faq.a: Yes, if you choose a saw head that fits Jameson poles.

name: Jameson Big Mouth Pulley Pruner
title: Jameson Big Mouth Pruner: Pulley Pole Pruner Head
meta: The Jameson Big Mouth pruner is a pulley pole pruner head with a wide jaw for larger stems. Pulley leverage makes overhead cuts easier on arms and shoulders.
tagline: A wide-jaw pole pruner head with pulley leverage for bigger overhead cuts.
summary: The Jameson Big Mouth pruner is a pulley pole pruner head with a wider jaw than a standard head. The pulley multiplies your pull on the rope, so cutting larger stems overhead takes less effort.
highlights: Wide jaw takes larger stems
Pulley for added cutting leverage
Fits Jameson pole systems
Replaceable blade, spring and hardware

p: A pole pruner without a pulley relies on your arm strength through a straight pull. Adding a pulley gives mechanical advantage, so the same pull delivers more force at the blade. On bigger stems near the top of the head's capacity, that is the difference between one clean cut and a stuck blade.
Paired with the Big Mouth's wider opening, it is a strong choice for lifting canopies, clearing sidewalks and dropping small limbs off structures.
Keep the blade sharp and the pivot clean. Replace the return spring when the jaw stops opening briskly, and replace the rope when it frays or glazes. Check that the pulley turns freely.
Work clear of power lines unless qualified and using properly rated tools. For kits and other pole pruners, see our pruners and loppers range.

faq.q: Does the Big Mouth head come with a pole?
faq.a: The head is often sold on its own. Check the listing or choose a kit.

faq.q: Can I replace the Big Mouth spring myself?
faq.a: Yes. Replacement springs are available and swap in with basic tools.

name: Jameson CompositLock Big Mouth Pruner
title: Jameson CompositLock Big Mouth Pruner Head
meta: Jameson CompositLock Big Mouth pruner head, a wide-jaw pole pruner made for Jameson's CompositLock pole system. Bigger bites overhead with a secure pole joint.
tagline: The wide-jaw Big Mouth pole pruner, set up for Jameson's CompositLock poles.
summary: The Jameson CompositLock Big Mouth pruner is the wide-jaw Big Mouth pole pruner head made to fit Jameson's CompositLock pole connection. If your kit runs CompositLock poles, this is the Big Mouth version that mounts directly.
highlights: Big Mouth wide-jaw pruner head
Made for Jameson CompositLock poles
Rope-operated with pulley leverage
Replaceable blade and spring

p: Pole tools are only as good as their connections. Jameson offers heads for different pole fittings, and the CompositLock version of the Big Mouth is for crews whose poles use that system. Matching head and pole avoids adapters and the play that comes with them.
The Big Mouth jaw takes larger stems than a standard pruner head, so you can handle more cuts before switching to a pole saw.
Seat the hook fully over the limb before pulling, and cut just outside the branch collar. Keep the blade sharp, clean sap off after use and replace the spring and rope when they wear.
Confirm your poles use the CompositLock connection before ordering. Never work near energized lines without qualification and rated tools. Compare other heads in our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: Will this head fit my older Jameson poles?
faq.a: Only if they use the CompositLock connection. Check your pole fitting before ordering.

faq.q: Is the blade the same as a standard Big Mouth?
faq.a: Check the parts list for your head. Replacement parts are listed by model.

name: Jameson Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
title: Jameson Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
h1: Jameson Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
meta: Jameson pulley pruner head with pole adapter and pull rope included. Mount it on your poles and start cutting overhead with the added leverage of a pulley.
tagline: A complete pulley pole pruner head with adapter and rope, ready to mount.
summary: This Jameson pulley pruner comes with the pole adapter and pull rope, so it is ready to mount on a compatible pole. The pulley adds leverage to every pull for cleaner overhead cuts with less effort.
highlights: Pulley pole pruner head
Pole adapter included
Pull rope included
Ready to mount on compatible poles

p: Buying just a head often means a second order for an adapter and rope. This version includes both, so if you already have poles, you can fit the head, run the rope and get to work. It is a good way to add a pruner to a pole saw setup or replace a worn head on an existing kit.
The pulley gives a mechanical advantage over a straight pull, which matters on the bigger stems and on long days overhead.
Fit the adapter to your top pole section, mount the head and route the rope so it runs freely down the pole without wrapping. Check that the blade opens fully and closes cleanly before use.

Replace the rope when it frays, and the spring when the blade slows. Pole tools near power lines require qualified workers and rated tools. For more heads and kits, see our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: Will the adapter fit my poles?
faq.a: Check the adapter's fitting and diameter against your poles before ordering.

faq.q: How long is the included rope?
faq.a: Rope length varies by listing. Make sure it suits the total pole length you run.

name: Marvin Bull Pruner with Adapter
title: Marvin Bull Pruner with Adapter: Heavy Pole Pruner
meta: The Marvin bull pruner is a heavy-duty pole pruner head, supplied here with the pole adapter. Built for bigger, tougher cuts overhead on clearance and orchard work.
tagline: Marvin's heavy-duty pole pruner head, supplied with the pole adapter.
summary: The Marvin bull pruner is a heavy-duty pole pruner head made for tougher, larger cuts than a standard head. This version includes the adapter, so it is ready to mount on a compatible pole.
highlights: Heavy-duty Marvin pole pruner head
Pole adapter included
Rope-operated bypass cut
Built for demanding clearance and orchard pruning

p: Marvin pruners have long been a staple on orchard and clearance crews. The bull pruner is the heavier version, made for the cuts that stall a standard head. If your work involves a lot of thick stems overhead, the stouter build pays off in fewer stuck blades and less wear.
Including the adapter means you can fit it straight to your pole instead of ordering parts separately.

Mount the adapter on the top pole section, fit the head and run the pull rope clean down the pole. Keep the blade sharp, clean off sap and oil the pivot. Replace the spring, hardware and rope as they wear, using Marvin parts.
Do not work near energized lines unless qualified and using rated tools. More pole pruners are in our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Marvin bull pruner and the standard Marvin pruner?
faq.a: The bull pruner is the heavier-duty head for bigger cuts. The standard head is lighter for general pruning.

faq.q: Does it come with rope?
faq.a: This version includes the adapter. Check the listing for rope.

name: Marvin Pruner with Adapter
title: Marvin Pruner with Adapter: Pole Pruner Head
meta: The Marvin pruner is a classic rope-operated pole pruner head, supplied with the pole adapter. A dependable choice for general overhead pruning from the ground.
tagline: A classic Marvin pole pruner head supplied with its pole adapter.
summary: The Marvin pruner is a rope-operated pole pruner head for general overhead pruning, supplied here with the adapter that mounts it to a pole. It is a simple, durable tool that crews have relied on for years.
highlights: Rope-operated bypass pole pruner
Pole adapter included
Lighter than the Marvin bull pruner
Replaceable spring, blade and hardware

p: For lifting canopies, clearing suckers and trimming small limbs overhead, a standard pole pruner is the quickest tool on the truck. The Marvin head is simple: a bypass blade, a hook, a spring and a rope. Fewer parts means fewer things to go wrong, and everything that does wear can be replaced.
With the adapter included, you can fit it straight to a compatible pole.

Seat the hook fully, then pull with a smooth stroke. Cut just outside the branch collar and avoid stubs. For limbs at the edge of capacity, step up to a pole saw or the Marvin bull pruner rather than forcing it.
Keep the blade sharp and the pivot oiled. Replace the spring when the blade slows. Work clear of power lines unless qualified with rated tools. Browse our pruners and loppers range for more.

faq.q: Which spring does the Marvin pruner use?
faq.a: Check your Marvin parts list. The PH4 spring is a common replacement for Marvin pruner heads.

faq.q: Can I fit this head on Jameson poles?
faq.a: Only if the adapter matches the pole diameter and fitting. Check before ordering.

name: Pole Pruner Braided Polyester Cord
title: Pole Pruner Rope: Braided Polyester Cord
meta: Braided polyester pole pruner rope for replacing a frayed or glazed pull cord. Low stretch for a crisp cut and a firm grip on every pull overhead.
tagline: Replacement braided polyester pull cord for pole pruners.
summary: This braided polyester pole pruner rope replaces the pull cord on a pole pruner head. Polyester stretches little, so more of your pull goes into the cut, and the braid gives a firm grip.
highlights: Braided polyester construction
Low stretch for a crisp cut
Firm grip for gloved hands
Replaces frayed or glazed pull cords

p: The pull cord takes friction through the pulley, abrasion along the pole and plenty of UV. Once it frays, glazes or gets stiff, it slips through gloves and drags in the pulley. A worn cord can also snap mid-cut, leaving the blade stuck in a limb overhead.
Polyester holds up well to sun and wear and stretches less than nylon, so the cut feels crisp rather than spongy.

Check the cord diameter against your pruner's pulley and attachment point. Thread it through the head the same way as the old rope, tie it off per the manufacturer's instructions and cut it to length for your longest pole setup. Seal the cut end so it doesn't unravel.
This is a pull cord, not life-support rope. Never use it for climbing or rigging. See more pole pruners and parts in our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: What diameter cord do I need?
faq.a: Match the diameter your pruner head and pulley are designed for. Check the old cord or the maker's specs.

faq.q: Can I use climbing rope offcuts instead?
faq.a: Usually not. Climbing rope is often too thick for pruner pulleys and stretches more than a polyester pull cord.

name: ART SpiderJack 2.1 Dyneema
title: ART SpiderJack 2.1 Dyneema: MRS Friction Device
meta: The ART SpiderJack is a mechanical friction device for moving rope systems. This 2.1 Dyneema version gives smooth, adjustable control for working through the canopy.
tagline: A mechanical friction hitch for moving rope systems from ART.
summary: The ART SpiderJack is a mechanical friction device that replaces a friction hitch on a moving rope system (MRS). This 2.1 Dyneema version is an earlier generation of the SpiderJack, known for smooth tending and adjustable friction.
highlights: Mechanical friction device for MRS climbing
Replaces a traditional friction hitch
Adjustable friction for different ropes and loads
Smooth slack tending while moving through the canopy
Earlier SpiderJack generation; check current model availability

p: On a moving rope system, the friction hitch is what you control your descent and positioning with. A mechanical device like the SpiderJack does the same job without a cord that glazes and wears. Climbers like how it tends slack and how predictably it grabs and releases, especially on long working days.
Being mechanical, it behaves the same from one climb to the next, as long as it is set up correctly and matched to your rope.

Check the rope diameter range and compatible connectors in ART's instructions before use, and confirm the device suits your rope. Inspect the device, the Dyneema components and all connectors before every climb, and retire parts that show wear or damage.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before using it aloft.

faq.q: Can the SpiderJack be used for SRS?
faq.a: This device is designed for moving rope systems. Follow ART's instructions for approved configurations only.

faq.q: Is the SpiderJack 2.1 the current model?
faq.a: ART has released newer SpiderJack versions. Check availability and parts support before buying.

name: ISC Chipmunk Flex Tether
title: ISC Chipmunk Flex Tether: SRS Device Tether
meta: ISC Chipmunk flex tether for connecting and aligning the ISC Chipmunk in an SRS climbing system. Replace a worn tether to keep the device tending cleanly.
tagline: A replacement flexible tether for the ISC Chipmunk in SRS setups.
summary: The ISC Chipmunk flex tether connects the ISC Chipmunk to the rest of an SRS climbing system and holds it in alignment. A worn or damaged tether should be replaced before it affects how the system behaves.
highlights: Flexible tether for the ISC Chipmunk
Keeps the device aligned in an SRS system
Replacement for a worn or damaged tether
Follow ISC's configuration instructions

p: In SRS setups, how components connect affects how they tend and how they load. A flexible tether keeps a device positioned without making the system stiff. Over time tethers abrade, get stiff with sap and grit, or get cut, and they need replacing.
Using the correct tether for the device keeps the system configured the way the manufacturer tested it.

Install the tether exactly as ISC's instructions show for the Chipmunk, with approved connectors. Inspect it before every climb for cuts, fuzzing, glazing and stiffness, and retire it at the first sign of damage.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before using it aloft. Compare other SRS climbing devices for your setup.

faq.q: Can I use a generic sling instead of the flex tether?
faq.a: Use the tether ISC specifies for the Chipmunk. Substitutes can change how the system loads and behaves.

faq.q: How often should I replace the tether?
faq.a: Inspect it before every climb and replace it whenever it shows wear, damage or stiffness, or as ISC recommends.

name: Rope Runner (Vertec)
title: Rope Runner SRS Climbing Device
meta: The Rope Runner is a mechanical friction device for stationary rope systems, with smooth descent control and good slack tending for working and moving in the tree.
tagline: A mechanical friction device for stationary rope tree climbing.
summary: The Rope Runner is a mechanical friction device built for stationary rope systems (SRS). It gives smooth descent control and tends slack well, so climbers can ascend, work and move laterally on a single tied-off line.
highlights: Mechanical friction device for SRS
Smooth, controllable descent
Good slack tending when paired with a pulley
Popular for production climbing

p: SRS climbing changed how a lot of arborists work big trees, and devices like the Rope Runner are a big part of that. It sits on the rope at the bridge, gives controlled friction for descent and lets you move around the canopy on a stationary line. Paired with a hitch tending pulley and a foot ascender, it is a full working system.
The appeal is consistency: the device behaves the same climb to climb, without the wear and adjustment of a friction hitch.

Check the rope diameter range and approved connectors in the manufacturer's instructions before use. Set it up exactly as shown, and do a ground test before leaving the ground. Inspect the device for wear on friction surfaces before each climb.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before using it aloft. Browse other SRS climbing devices to compare.

faq.q: Can the Rope Runner be used on a moving rope system?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for approved configurations. It is designed primarily for SRS.

faq.q: What rope works with the Rope Runner?
faq.a: Check the instructions for approved rope diameters and constructions before climbing.

name: CAMP Tree Access Evo
title: CAMP Tree Access Evo: Arborist Climbing Saddle
meta: The CAMP Tree Access Evo is a European-style arborist saddle with a bridge attachment, built for comfort on long climbs and for both MRS and SRS work in the tree.
tagline: A European-style bridge saddle from CAMP for full-day tree work.
summary: The CAMP Tree Access Evo is a European-style arborist climbing saddle built around a bridge attachment. It is made for climbers who spend long hours in the tree and want a saddle that moves well and supports them in a working position.
highlights: European-style bridge saddle
Built for full-day working comfort
Suits MRS and SRS climbing
Gear loops and attachment points for tools
Check sizing and replaceable parts

p: A bridge lets your climbing system slide side to side as you turn, so you can face your work without twisting against the tie-in. That freedom, plus a well-padded waist and leg loops, is why many production climbers favor European-style saddles for long days in the canopy.
The Tree Access Evo is CAMP's take on that design, with attachment points for lanyards, chainsaws and tools.
Get the size right. The saddle should sit snug at the waist with the leg loops adjusted so you hang comfortably without pressure points. Hang-test in it before climbing.

Inspect the bridge, stitching, webbing and buckles before each use, and replace the bridge and other wear parts as CAMP directs. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before using it aloft.

faq.q: Can I replace the bridge on the Tree Access Evo?
faq.a: Bridges are wear items. Use CAMP's replacement parts and follow its instructions and retirement guidance.

faq.q: Is the Tree Access Evo good for SRS?
faq.a: Bridge saddles suit both MRS and SRS. Pair it with a chest harness if your SRS setup calls for one.
